passages.note: Vote page shows Aguiar-Curry voted Aye on concurrence in Senate amendments to AB 2097.

passages.provision_quote: A public agency shall not impose or enforce any minimum automobile parking requirement on a residential, commercial, or other development project if the project is located within one-half mile of public transit.
passages.note: Enacted text bars most local minimum parking mandates near transit, the opposite of rung 5's abundant-parking premise.

rows.reasoning: Aguiar-Curry voted Aye on AB 2097 (2021-2022), which bars a public agency from imposing minimum parking requirements near transit, the opposite of rung 5's foundation of 'abundant free parking.' Removing a parking mandate shows a direction away from parking-centric policy but does not itself fund or prioritize 'pedestrian infrastructure, cycling networks, and public transit' or any other named clause of rungs 1 through 4, so no numbered rung is chair-shaped.
